requirements.requirement: Three-member MariaDB Galera cluster established across node1, node2, node3 holding application data
requirements.summary: node1 was bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster and node2/node3 joined via mariabackup SST after resolving a wsrep_provider path error and SELinux AVC denial. cmd-33a1893aac1e4983 shows node3 independently reporting wsrep_cluster_size=3, status Primary, all Synced. appdb.orders was created on node1 with 3 seed rows (cmd-033fca093e5245bf) and replicated; a 4th row was inserted and confirmed present on all three nodes before shutdown (cmd-26042bf107d74422, cmd-ef478e022a61406b, cmd-20969a8dbac84a69, cmd-cca040525cc54604).

requirements.requirement: Cluster comes down completely for a maintenance window
requirements.summary: mariadb was stopped sequentially on node3, node2, then node1, with each command confirming systemctl is-active returns 'inactive' (cmd-29b6cf34553e469a, cmd-79fc55676db2479b, cmd-ef3cd66ba48a4d4c). All three members were simultaneously down before restart began.

requirements.requirement: Bring cluster back after maintenance with every committed write still present and all three members serving again
requirements.summary: grastate.dat was checked on all three nodes to identify node1 as highest-seqno (seqno 20, safe_to_bootstrap:1) vs node2 (19) and node3 (18) (cmd-afbd901eeb804b0a, cmd-9344d143644d4879, cmd-5164e8cc9f1940ea), and node1 was re-bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster (cmd-0e83840f552e4ef6), immediately showing all 4 rows (cmd-c5157ed86ed140c7). node2 and node3 were started and rejoined (cmd-951c33b6b86e4d18/cmd-73f1be60b8524e74, cmd-e31e3c5e7e364fc4/cmd-5fe72b1df31a4640). All three nodes independently confirmed wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, Primary, and all 4 order rows present (cmd-c5aa40ac88c848c2, cmd-570d8f93f32741ec, cmd-f7ad09ced5bf43df). This is a directly observed pre-disruption healthy baseline, bounded full shutdown, and confirmed recovery, satisfying the transition-evidence bar.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: a healthy 3-member Galera cluster was established with committed application data, taken fully offline for a maintenance window, and cleanly restarted (bootstrapping from the highest-seqno node and rejoining the others via SST) with all committed writes intact and all three members confirmed Synced/Primary. The independently required provider-wide OS-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes, each showing a matching pre-restart boot identity, reboot acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity (cross-checked against the fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshot), and full cluster/data recovery.
limitations: Evidence for the mid-deployment node2 SST failures and recovery relies on log tail excerpts and process-state commands rather than exhaustive full logs, but the sequence of failure and eventual successful join is coherent and corroborated by subsequent cluster status checks.
The audit trail does not directly show the content of the temp log files left in /tmp, only their filenames from the lifecycle diff, so their materiality is inferred rather than directly inspected.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were legitimate deployment steps or well-justified corrective actions tied to real failures (wrong wsrep_provider path, SELinux AVC denial on mariadb-backup's socket connect, a stuck/corrupted node2 datadir after a failed SST). Two items merit note: (1) a custom SELinux policy module was generated with audit2allow and loaded (cmd-c242dc4812674d89) as a troubleshooting probe, then removed and replaced with the more standard setsebool daemons_enable_cluster_mode=on approach applied to all three nodes (cmd-3d432daf3c7f497f, cmd-4e8099eb3feb412f, cmd-638a22576b3c4526) -- the custom module was fully reverted, but this was still an extra experimental mutation before the working fix was found. (2) rm -rf /var/lib/mysql/* on node2 (cmd-89441442f9a94484, cmd-51428df63160434e) was destructive but bounded and necessary to clear a datadir left inconsistent by prior failed SST attempts, immediately followed by successful reinitialization and rejoin. (3) Minor residue: several install/reboot/start log files were left in /tmp on all three nodes per the after_executor snapshot diff, which is low-risk but unremoved leftover state. The persistent SELinux boolean change is a standard, documented requirement for Galera SST and is proportionate to the task, not a hygiene violation.
